svg.title: PD over TCP vs InfiniBand RDMA, fixed-shape sweep
svg.desc: Small-multiple line charts comparing aggregated serving, PD over TCP and PD over InfiniBand RDMA across concurrency 1, 4, 8 and 16 on four fixed shapes for TTFT p50 (ms, log scale) and output throughput (tok/s, linear). In this separate follow-up with larger-than-default KV blocks, RDMA PD observes lower long-prompt TTFT p50 and higher throughput than TCP PD (for example, 1,966.856 vs 8,065.377 ms and 475.153 vs 194.074 tok/s on 4096/128 concurrency 16), while aggregated serving still leads both long-prompt concurrency-16 cells and TCP PD keeps lower TTFT p50 at 512/256 concurrency 8 and 16 and 256/1024 concurrency 16.
svg.text: MODEL DEPLOYMENT · PD BENCHMARK · RDMA FOLLOW-UP
PD over TCP vs InfiniBand RDMA, fixed-shape sweep
One node with 8 × H100 SXM5 and 8 × ConnectX-7 InfiniBand adapters; same roles, TP = 2 per replica.
PD over InfiniBand RDMA, same roles
The RDMA run is a separate follow-up with the same shapes and request counts, 640/640 requests, zero errors. It used larger KV blocks than the engine default.
Aggregated and PD over TCP values repeat the baseline run. Separate runs and small prompt-length variations prevent a transport-only causal claim.
